requirements.requirement: Run an LDAP directory on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test and import the staged LDIF while preserving the supplied user identities and mail addresses.
requirements.summary: Node1 serves LDAP on port 389 with the requested suffix. The imported and post-restart directory contains alex/Alex North/alex@branch.test and sam/Sam West/sam@branch.test, matching the observed staged LDIF; the staged file's executor-observed checksum also remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree on node1 and find both users.
requirements.summary: Direct searches from node2 returned both expected users before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Directory updates require authenticated administrator access, and anonymous writes fail.
requirements.summary: An authenticated administrator modification succeeded, was directly observed, and was reverted. Anonymous modifications from node2 were rejected with LDAP error 8 both before and after restart, with no test attribute left behind.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The final node1 state remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic and used the distribution-compatible OpenLDAP 2.3.35 packages. Fixed lifecycle observations also show the same kernel before preparation and after execution on both nodes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Node1 serves the imported directory with the supplied user data intact, node2 finds both users, administrator writes work while anonymous writes fail, and the legacy OS and kernel were retained. Both managed nodes also completed the provider-wide restart protocol successfully. Operational hygiene is reduced by two reverted configuration experiments and retained pre-import backup artifacts.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle collector reports listening-socket inventories as empty and cannot assess failed services because systemctl is unsupported on this legacy release; direct executor commands nevertheless show slapd listening and working after restart.
No final command inventories the pre-import backup paths, so their continued presence is inferred from their creation and the absence of captured cleanup.

The preparation baseline used SHA-256 while executor checks used MD5, preventing a same-algorithm before/after checksum comparison; staged contents and final LDAP attributes were directly observed and coherent.

operational_hygiene.summary: The final service and package state was healthy, and the required restart protocol was complete for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered LDAP data/client behavior. Hygiene deductions apply to two unnecessary, restored troubleshooting mutations: cmd-aa12d2ed132a4be5 temporarily introduced duplicate rootdn/rootpw directives before cmd-16e71e681299453e restored and corrected the configuration; cmd-dfe5ef5b73cb410e temporarily replaced the hashed root password with plaintext and restarted slapd, then cmd-36d8d1f09d7f4275 restored hashed storage. Both were bounded and reverted, but the plaintext interval briefly weakened credential storage. Necessary rollback backups created by cmd-aa12d2ed132a4be5, cmd-0921385efc244b00, and cmd-1613e729a9664600 appear to have been retained as /etc/ldap/slapd.conf.preimport, /root/slapd.preimport.ldif, and /var/lib/ldap.preimport; no cleanup is captured, leaving probable post-task backup residue. No executor-created /tmp residue or damaged package state was observed.
